result.title: Power-Law Correlations Without Apparent Temperature-Tuned Criticality in Fixed-Tree Hierarchical Languages
result.summary: Sampling temperature can substantially reshape autoregressive generation, but it is unclear when temperature changes in long-range correlations reflect a genuine phase transition rather than a smooth change in statistics. We study this question in a controlled analogue of temperature sampling: a finite-depth probabilistic context-free grammar on a fixed hierarchical tree, where exact next-token conditionals are computed by belief propagation and then rescaled by a softmax temperature before autoregressive sampling. We measure two-point mutual information between tokens as a function of separation. Across the tested temperatures and grammar ensembles, mutual information remains well described by a power-law envelope. Temperature changes the correlation magnitude and fitted exponent, but within the accessible system sizes we find no long-distance plateau characteristic of an ordered phase and no clear crossover to short-range exponential decay. An approximate mapping to an Ising model on a tree explains how exponential decay in tree distance becomes a power law in token distance, allowing power laws to persist without tuning to a special decoding temperature. This controlled baseline clarifies which temperature effects can arise from hierarchical structure alone, before adding training, approximation error, or neural architecture.

AI.brief_summary: 该文在固定层次树上的概率上下文无关文法中，用信念传播得到精确的下一词条件分布并按温度缩放后自回归采样，测量两点互信息随距离的变化，发现在所测温度与文法集合下互信息始终呈幂律包络，既无有序相的长程平台也无明显的短程指数衰减转折，并用树上的 Ising 近似解释树距离上的指数衰减如何变成 token 距离上的幂律。
AI.relevance_reason: 这是一项与视觉多模态推理无关的受控玩具模型研究，但其结论提示「长程幂律相关或临界性可能只是层次结构的产物、无需特殊解码温度」，这一警示性基线可能可供核查 LVR 中对 latent 状态长程相关、深度位置效应或相变式涌现解读的评价。
